verdict: Caution: lend selectively to re-rollers with own working-capital discipline and a Tata-linked or branded TMT outlet; avoid pure conversion units dependent on one buyer and thin GST-paid inventory.
title: Ludhiana steel re-rolling & TMT: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A Ludhiana re-roller buys billets or scrap, heats and rolls them into TMT bars, and sells to builders, contractors and stockists. **Cash is made on the spread between input and finished steel, not on volume alone, so the whole credit case rests on how fast that spread converts to cash.** The cycle is short and brutal: inventory is priced daily, receivables run 30-60 days, and a 5% GST on steel is what the industry is lobbying for to free MSME working capital [1]. **So when a proposal lands, check the GST-paid purchase trail and the finished-goods holding days; if inventory days exceed the payable cycle, ask why the unit is funding steel it has already sold.**

## What has changed in Ludhiana
Tata Steel commissioned a ₹3,200-cr green steel plant in Ludhiana in March 2026, with 2,500 jobs expected [2][3]. **That is a structural change: local billet supply improves, but it also pulls the best buyers and skilled labour toward a large, credit-strong anchor.** Punjab GST collections grew 9.7% Apr-to-date versus India's 6.1% [D], a genuine local tailwind, while electricity demand grew 8.8% versus India's 9.5% [D] — neutral. **So pursue units that can show they are selling into that stronger local GST base; if a borrower's sales growth is below the state GST trend, ask which customers they lost.**

## Where the growth is
Peer results are strong: Steel Exchange India clocked ~₹340 crore revenue in Q2 FY27, up ~45% YoY [6], and Rathi Steel grew over 30% YoY with ~28.86% volume growth [7]. JSW Steel reported 20% EBITDA margin and gearing of 0.42 [5]. **The growth is in branded TMT with a dealer network, not in commodity re-rolling.** Pursue re-rollers who supply the Tata plant's downstream or hold a regional TMT brand; avoid single-furnace converters selling to one stockist. **If a proposal is a conversion job for one buyer, ask for the buyer's payment history before sanctioning.**

## How to grow safely
Structure term debt against the rolling mill only, keep working capital as a separate cash-credit line, and take monthly stock and receivable statements. **Take GST returns, e-way bills and electricity bills every month — power consumption is the honest proxy for rolling days.** Rating reports flag sudden price swings hitting margins [10] and moderately high working-capital needs [11]. **So covenant a maximum inventory-to-sales ratio and a minimum interest coverage; if coverage falls below the peer gearing benchmark of 1.80x [10], ask for a stock audit before any enhancement.**

## Early warning signs
Watch for falling rolling days, rising receivable days, and a shift from branded to commodity sales. **If a borrower's e-way bills drop while GST sales stay flat, ask whether goods are moving outside the GST net.** Old rating reports (2023-24) [8][9] are dated; treat them as background only. **If a unit's power bill falls two months running, ask for the order book before renewing the limit.**
